info.description:
The Epinio server API, used by the CLI, the dashboard and the MCP server.

Requests authenticate with Basic Auth. Lifecycle
requests (stage, deploy, restart, update, source patch, and changes that
redeploy bound apps) answer 202 with an operation; poll AppState until
the operation is done.

Works for both deployed and never-deployed (create|build) apps.

patch.description:
The multipart body carries the source archive and an optional
`process_cmd` form field (supervisor fallback command for non-Paketo
buildpacks). Answers 202 with an operation that already carries the
`stage_id`; it builds and swaps the new image into the running pod.
patch.summary: Replace the source of the named `App` in the `Namespace` and rebuild it.

post.description:
Starts a build operation and answers 202 with it. The source is the
uploaded `blobuid`, else the stored blob, else the git origin, which the
server clones and stamps with the resolved branch and commit. Poll
AppState until the operation is done; its `stage_id` names the build
for the staging logs. The build does not deploy.
post.summary: Build an image for the named `App` in the `Namespace`.

get.description:
One call for status, build status, current stage and the latest
operation. While an operation stages or deploys, `status` reports that
phase. `operation` is absent after a server restart or once the record
of a finished operation expired.

post.description:
The multipart body carries the tar archive plus `mode` ("files" or

APIError.title: APIError fulfills the error and APIErrors interfaces. It contains a single error.

App.description:
The main structure has identifying information.
It is used in the CLI and API responses.
App.title: App has all the application's properties, for at rest (Configuration), and active (Workload).

buildstatus.description:
BuildStatus is "create", "build", or "deployed", reflecting the last
completed lifecycle step: create (empty app), build (stage), or deploy.
See AppBuildStatusCreate / AppBuildStatusBuild / AppBuildStatusDeployed.

built_image_url.description:
BuiltImageURL is the image produced by the last build (stage). It is
kept apart from ImageURL, which is the image currently deployed.

AppChart.description:
Differences:
Field `Values` is not made public here. It contains server-internal information the
user has no need for.
AppChart.title:
AppChart nearly matches github.com/epinio/application/api/v1 AppChartSpec
Reason for existence: Do not expose the internal CRD struct in the API.

AppChartList.description: AppChartList is a collection of app charts

AppChartPushResponse.description:
AppChartPushResponse is the server's response to a successful push of a chart archive. It
names the application chart created for the pushed chart, and where the chart was stored.

AppDeployment.description:
AppDeployment contains all the information specific to an active
application, i.e. one with a deployment in the cluster.

AppList.description: AppList is a collection of app references

AppMatchResponse.description: AppMatchResponse contains the list of names for matching apps

AppOperation.description:
Every lifecycle write (stage, deploy, restart, update, source patch)
returns one with 202, and GET .../state reports the latest.
AppOperation.title: AppOperation is one asynchronous lifecycle action on an application.

AppRef.description: AppRef references an App by name and namespace

AppScaleReport.title: AppScaleReport represents app creation and scaling metadata.

AppState.description:
AppState is the response of GET .../applications/:app/state: the
application's lifecycle state in one call. Status is the one field to
read: while an operation is staging or deploying it reports that phase,
otherwise it is the status derived from the App CR and the workload.
Operation is nil when this server holds no record of a recent operation
(after a restart, after the record expired, or on another replica).

ApplicationConfiguration.description: ApplicationConfiguration is the part of the manifest describing the configuration of the application

bound_configurations.description:
BoundConfigurations is read-only. It mirrors Configurations, adding the type
of each. It is exported into the manifest for information only: `epinio push`
binds from Configurations, and editing this list in a manifest has no effect.

ApplicationCreateRequest.description:
ApplicationCreateRequest represents and contains the data needed to
create an application (at rest), possibly with presets (configurations)

ApplicationDeleteResponse.description: ApplicationDeleteResponse represents the server's response to a successful app deletion

ApplicationOrigin.description:
ApplicationOrigin is the part of the manifest describing the origin of the application
(sources). At most one of the fields may be specified / not empty.

Kind.description:
Hidden from yaml. Type tag to simplify struct usage.
Note: we cannot hide this property from the JSON since it's used to unmarshal correctly the result of the Apps endpoint
@see failling test here: https://github.com/epinio/epinio/runs/4935898437?check_suite_focus=true
We should probably expose a more meaningful value instead of this "Kind" int

ApplicationStage.description:
ApplicationStage is the part of the manifest holding information
relevant to staging the application's sources.

ApplicationUpdateRequest.description:
ApplicationUpdateRequest represents and contains the data needed to update
an application. Specifically to modify the number of replicas to
run, and the configurations bound to it.
Note: Instances is a pointer to give us a nil value separate from
actual integers, as means of communicating `default`/`no change`.

AppsPage.title: AppsPage is one namespace's page of applications.

BindRequest.title: BindRequest represents and contains the data needed to bind configurations to an application.

BindResponse.description:
BindResponse represents the server's response to the successful binding of configurations to
an application.

BoundConfiguration.description:
BoundConfiguration names a configuration bound to an application, together with
its type ("custom" or "service"), so clients can tell configurations a user made
from ones a service created.

BuilderImage.description:
BuilderImage is the REST DTO for the BuilderImage CRD
(application.epinio.io/v1, kind BuilderImage). The CRD shape is intentionally
not re-exported here — we keep a domain wrapper so CRD revisions do not
become breaking client changes.

bound_apps.description:
BoundApps reports whether at least one application is currently staged
with this builder image. Read-only, computed from live app resources.

default.description:
Default reports whether this builder image is the cluster default.
Read-only: it is set as operator policy (helm seed / kubectl), never
through the create or update API.

BuilderImageCreateRequest.description:
BuilderImageCreateRequest carries the fields a client supplies when creating
a builder image. Name is required and lands in metadata.name; the remainder
land under spec.

BuilderImageList.description: BuilderImageList is a collection of builder images

BuilderImageMatchResponse.description: BuilderImageMatchResponse contains the list of names for matching builder images

BuilderImageUpdateRequest.description:
BuilderImageUpdateRequest carries optional field updates. Empty fields are
ignored — name is taken from the URL, not the body.

CatalogMatchResponse.description: CatalogMatchResponse contains the list of names for matching catalog entries

CatalogService.description:
CatalogService mostly matches github.com/epinio/application/api/v1 ServiceSpec
Reason for existence: Do not expose the internal CRD struct in the API.

bound_services.description:
BoundServices reports whether at least one provisioned service instance
derives from this catalog service. Read-only, computed from live service
instances. Named for what actually binds to a catalog service (instances),
not apps, which attach to instances rather than the catalog entry.

CatalogServiceUpdateRequest.description:
CatalogServiceUpdateRequest carries optional field updates. Empty string
fields are ignored — name is taken from the URL, not the body. Settings
and SecretTypes are replaced when non-nil; pass nil to leave untouched.

CatalogServices.description: CatalogServices is a list of catalog service elements

ChartMatchResponse.description: ChartMatchResponse contains the list of names for matching application charts

ChartSetting.description:
ChartSetting matches github.com/epinio/application/api/v1 ChartSetting
Reason for existence: Do not expose the internal CRD struct in the API.

enum.description: Enumeration of allowed values, for types string, number, integer

maximum.description: Maximal allowed value, for number, integer

minimum.description: Minimal allowed value, for number, integer

type.description: Type of the setting (string, bool, number, or integer)

ChartValueSettings.description:
ChartValueSettings is a collection of key/value pairs describing the user's chosen settings with which
to configure the helm chart referenced by the application's appchart.

ClusterReport.title: ClusterReport represents a cluster section in the report.

ConfigurationCreateRequest.description:
ConfigurationCreateRequest represents and contains the data needed to
create a configuration instance

ConfigurationDeleteRequest.description: ConfigurationDeleteRequest represents and contains the data needed to delete a configuration

ConfigurationDeleteResponse.description: ConfigurationDeleteResponse represents the server's response to a successful configuration deletion

ConfigurationMatchResponse.description: ConfigurationMatchResponse contains the list of names for matching configurations

ConfigurationRef.description: ConfigurationRef references a Configuration by name and namespace

ConfigurationReplaceRequest.description:
ConfigurationReplaceRequest represents and contains the data needed to
replace a configuration instance

ConfigurationResponse.description: ConfigurationResponse represents the data of a single configuration instance

ConfigurationResponseList.description: ConfigurationResponseList represents a collection of configuration instance

ConfigurationShowResponse.description: ConfigurationShowResponse contains details about a configuration

ConfigurationUpdateRequest.description:
ConfigurationUpdateRequest represents and contains the data needed to
update a configuration instance (add/change, and remove keys)

DeployRequest.description:
POST .../deploy is asynchronous and answers 202 with an AppOperation.
It deploys ImageURL when set (Stage names the build that produced it).
Otherwise it builds first: from BlobUID, from the stored blob, or by
cloning a git Origin, then deploys the result.
DeployRequest.title:
DeployRequest represents and contains the data needed to deploy an application
Note that the overall application configuration (instances, configurations, EVs) is
already known server side, through AppCreate/AppUpdate requests.
This request not only comes with the image to deploy, but also the
information where the sources of that image came from.

EnvMatchResponse.description: EnvMatchResponse contains the list of names for matching env variables

EnvVariable.description: EnvVariable represents the Show Response for a single environment variable

EnvVariableGroupedResponse.description: EnvVariableGroupedResponse represents environment variables grouped by their origin

EnvVariableMap.description:
EnvVariableMap is a collection of EVs as a map. It is used for Set Requests, and as
List Responses

EnvVariableOrigin.description: EnvVariableOrigin represents the source of an environment variable

ErrorResponse.description: ErrorResponse is the response's JSON, that is send in case of an error

ExportregistriesListResponse.description: ExportregistriesListResponse contains the list of all known export registries

ExportregistriesMatchResponse.description: ExportregistriesMatchResponse contains the list of names for matching export registries

ExportregistryResponse.description: ExportregistryResponse contains the information for a single known export registry

Gitconfig.description:
Gitconfig contains the public parts of git.Configuration
Password and cert data are private and excluded.
TODO : Track creating user of the config.

bound_apps.description:
BoundApps reports whether at least one application currently references
this git configuration. Read-only, computed from live app resources.

GitconfigCreateRequest.title: GitconfigCreateRequest contains the data for a new git configuration.

GitconfigsMatchResponse.description: GitconfigsMatchResponse contains the list of names for matching git configurations

HelmRepo.description:
HelmRepo matches github.com/epinio/application/api/v1 HelmRepo
Reason for existence: Do not expose the internal CRD struct in the API.

HelmRepoRequest.description:
HelmRepoRequest mirrors the on-cluster CR HelmRepo, including the Secret
reference used to resolve credentials. Used by catalog service write
requests; auth values themselves are never accepted in the request body.

InfoResponse.description: InfoResponse contains information about Epinio and its components

MeResponse.description: MeResponse contains information about the current authenticated user

Meta.description:
Meta holds the information needed to reference a resource (name and namespace), plus
general descriptive things (creation timestamp).

MetaLite.title: MetaLite holds the information needed to reference a non-namespaced resource (name),

Namespace.description:
Namespace has all the namespace properties, i.e. name, app names, and configuration names
It is used in the CLI and API responses.

NamespaceCreateRequest.description: NamespaceCreateRequest contains the name of the namespace that should be created

NamespaceList.description: NamespaceList is a collection of namespaces

NamespacesMatchResponse.description: NamespacesMatchResponse contains the list of names for matching namespaces

NodeReport.title: NodeReport represents a single node row in the report.

OperationKind.title: OperationKind names the lifecycle action an AppOperation runs.

OperationPhase.description:
OperationPhase is the progress of an AppOperation. The values match the
status of the removed /deployments endpoint, so the UI keeps its labels.

OperationsResponse.description:
OperationsResponse reports the operations a request started, one per
application it redeployed, and the applications it skipped.

failure_reason.description:
FailureReason is non-empty when the pod will not become ready without
intervention: an image pull failure, a container config error, a crash
loop, or never having been scheduled.

ReportResponse.title: ReportResponse represents a rancher-like node report.

ServiceBatchBindRequest.description: ServiceBatchBindRequest represents a request to bind multiple services to an application at once

ServiceDeleteRequest.description: ServiceDeleteRequest represents and contains the data needed to delete a service

ServiceDeleteResponse.description: ServiceDeleteResponse represents the server's response to a successful service deletion

ServiceList.description: ServiceList represents a collection of service instances

ServiceMatchResponse.description: ServiceMatchResponse contains the list of names for matching services

ServiceReplaceRequest.description:
ServiceReplaceRequest represents and contains the data needed to
replace a service instance (i.e. the custom value keys)

ServiceUpdateRequest.description:
ServiceUpdateRequest represents and contains the data needed to
update a service instance (add/change, and remove custom value keys)

SkippedApp.description:
SkippedApp names an application a request could not start an operation
for, and why (usually: another operation is already running).

StageRef.description:
StageRef references a staging run by ID, currently randomly generated
for each POST to the staging endpoint

StageRequest.description: StageRequest represents and contains the data needed to stage an application

SystemPodReport.title: SystemPodReport represents a pod entry in the report header.

UploadResponse.description: UploadResponse represents the server's response to a successful app sources upload

ErrorResponse.description: The error body every failed request returns.
